newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds hold earlier gains, eye currencies.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds hold earlier gains, eye currencies.

text.p: Irish government bonds held on to earlier gains and kept pace with both Germany and the UK in thin late trade on Thursday as the market kept a close eye on currencies, dealers said.

"Things have been very quiet, with the States closed for the Thanksgiving Day holiday. We have managed to keep pace with both Germany and the UK but really there has not been a lot of action," one dealer said.
"At this stage people are keeping a close eye on the currencies, on convergence trade," the dealer added.
By 1602 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had gained 10 pence to 102.35 to yield 5.84 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 had risen 20 pence to 109.65 to yield 6.51 percent.
Dealers said the domestic market was likely to remain around its current levels into next week with the U.S. unlikely to see much action in Friday's post-holiday session.
